## Overview

The reverse-direction [LRP176](../lrp-rli-med-176) ($WR_{t2} \rightarrow LS_{t4}$) reads its indirect effect on the 0–32 letter-sound scale, which is ~12% ceilinged at t4 and could attenuate the NIE. LRP276 is the **ceiling-sensitivity companion**: the identical design with the outcome taken at **t3** (only ~6% of children at the $LS$ ceiling), so the reverse $WR \rightarrow LS$ indirect is read with more room in the outcome to move. Agreement describes stability across outcome horizons; a difference can reflect follow-up time, ceiling support or other model differences. Neither result isolates a ceiling effect.

## Design

Mediator $W_{t2}$ (Beta-Binomial on $W_{t1}$); outcome $L_{t3}$ (conditioned on $L_{t1}$, loaded via the lagged-outcome preparation). Adjustment $\{G, A, W_\text{pre}, W_{t1}, HS, SP\}$ — identical to [LRP176](../lrp-rli-med-176); only the outcome wave changes (t4 → t3).

## Assumptions — read this first {#sec-assumptions}

Assignment still randomises treatment schedules after crossover. It does not randomise word reading as a mediator, and latent ability and treatment-induced dose confounding remain. This decomposition assumes a reverse direction; it cannot establish that reading changes letter-sound knowledge. Compare its uncertainty with the t4-outcome companion. Changing the outcome wave changes both ceiling support and follow-up time, so the comparison does not isolate either influence.
